entities.name: PMID:25422292
observations: 2015 European Journal of Cardio-Thoracic Surgery study of shock wave therapy in decellularized porcine aortic xenografts implanted subcutaneously in C57BL/6 mice.
Shock wave therapy was delivered immediately after implantation at 0.1 mJ/mm², 500 impulses, and 5 Hz; grafts were assessed at 72 hours and 3 weeks.
Treated grafts had smaller calcification areas and enhanced recruitment of osteoclastic cells near calcified tissue.

Shock wave therapy altered rather than uniformly suppressed inflammation: macrophage infiltration and M2 polarization increased, graft TNF-α and IL-6 mRNA increased, while endothelial-cell CD40 ligand and complement C5/C5a decreased.
Authors interpreted reduced calcification as resulting from modulation of the acute macrophage-mediated inflammatory response.

entities.name: Shock wave therapy
observations: Physical treatment applied immediately after implantation in the PMID:25422292 mouse xenograft model at 0.1 mJ/mm², 500 impulses, and 5 Hz.

entities.name: Graft calcification
observations: Calcification of decellularized porcine aortic xenografts was reduced in shock-wave-treated mouse grafts compared with untreated controls in PMID:25422292.

entities.name: Inflammation-calcification modulation
observations: In decellularized aortic xenografts in mice, shock wave therapy altered acute macrophage-mediated inflammation and was accompanied by reduced calcification and increased osteoclastic-cell recruitment.
The inflammatory shift included increased macrophage infiltration and M2 polarization, so the mechanism was modulation rather than generalized anti-inflammatory suppression.
